transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-06
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Aurora Tech, Head of ML), Jason Muller (Aurora Tech, VP Eng), Nina Park (Aurora Tech, Infra), Samir (Aurora SRE)

Summary (auto): console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, batching and KV cache impacts on cost, and security/compliance next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood, with Liam our systems engineer. today's roughly 40 minutes, we'll do a short demo of the console, specifically the usage analytics and per-route dashboards and then a cost breakdown. afterwards we'll capture next steps.
[00:14] Priya: Hi, thanks. quick note, Our main ask is predictable cost and data residency, we run embeddings and small chat endpoints and worried about token surprices, right?
[00:27] Liam: Yep totally, and we'd like to show how the per-route dashboards break down tokens, latency, error rates, and routing so you can see what routes are costing you. also, batching/caching recommendations can reduce unit cost by a lot.
[00:41] Jason: Quick background — we have a mix of on-prem and cloud, about 300k requests/day for search embeddings, spikes to 1.2M/day on campaign days. sequence lengths vary but avg 512 for chat, embeddings smaller.
[00:59] Sofia: great context, thanks. timeline? are you looking to pilot Q1?
[01:05] Priya: Q1 pilot is the plan, security sign-off is the gating item.
[01:12] Liam: ok we'll make sure to push the SOC2 and ISO docs, and the dedicated capacity SLAs.
[01:20] [Screen share starts - Redwood Console]
[01:28] Liam: so here is the main usage analytics page, top-level metrics: total tokens, avg latency, errors, per-model usage. we can filter by route or model, date range. note that timestamps in this export are UTC, there may be slight timezone labelling quirks.
[01:44] Priya: looks good. can we break down costs by route — like embeddings vs chat?
[01:50] Liam: yes, the per-route dashboard does exactly that. clicking into 'embed-search' route here shows tokens in/out, per-token charge, and a calculated cost column. these costs are estimated based on the rate-card, and if you use Dedicated we can show effective unit costs after commit discounts.
[02:12] Samir: is that the same as batching savings? how do you account for batching/caching in the cost calc?
[02:18] Liam: good question. we estimate on two axes: effective tokens emitted and batching efficiency. if you enable continuous batching with a 200ms window for chat, you can get 15-30% token efficiency for certain workloads. also KV/prefix caching for repeated context reduces repeated input tokens. the console can simulate projected savings if you input your traffic profile.
[02:42] Jason: any gotchas when you have mixed on-prem and cloud? latency routing?
[02:48] Liam: we support smart routing by region and capacity tier; for mixed deployments you'd likely use Private or Dedicated in your VPC for the on-prem traffic and Hosted for public endpoints, with routing policies to keep PII in private. there is a small config nuance around KV cache locality — if you're on Private we localize cache to your cluster which helps latency.
[03:08] [00:03:15] Priya: is the per-route dashboard able to export CSV for our finance team?
[03:21] Liam: yes, export CSV and PDF are built-in, and you can also pull the raw usage API and join with your billing system. note: sometimes the export labels model names slightly differently, e.g., 'rw-llama-xl' might be transcribed as 'raw lama xl' in older exports.
[03:38] Priya: haha ok noted — transcription quirks.
[03:44] Sofia: next I'm going to jump to the finance view — cost breakdown by route. this is an example from a reference customer. you can see per-request avg tokens, per-token price, and projected monthly spend. we also surface a 'what-if' tool to model batching and quantization.
[04:06] Jason: that what-if tool — can you show the impact of 8-bit quantization for embeddings?
[04:12] Liam: yes, quantization reduces memory footprint and often allows cheaper instance types. the console will show a model-advice card: e.g., 8-bit quant -> 20% lower per-token infra cost for embeddings, but you should run evals for quality. it's a recommendation, not automatic.
[04:30] Nina: security — how do audit logs and KMS show up in the console? we need to prove key rotation and audit trails to our auditors.
[04:38] Liam: audit logs are exported to your cloud logging (CloudWatch/Stackdriver) or into the private control plane for Private deployments. KMS integration: we support customer-managed keys, and the console surfaces the key alias and last rotation date. for Dedicated we can provide more granular access logs.
[04:56] Priya: and SSO?
[05:00] Sofia: we support SAML/SSO, RBAC at route level. we'll include the SSO setup guide.
[05:06] [05:06] Jason: can we do an example route breakdown for our 'assistant-chat' and 'embed-search' — like show where tokens are coming from?
[05:15] Liam: yep clicking assistant-chat — you see inbound context tokens (user prompt + sys) vs generated tokens, avg latency, and a histogram of sequence length. this helps identify if your system is sending large system prompts that inflate costs.
[05:32] Priya: we've seen some clients accidentally include long system prompts — nice to see that.
[05:36] Liam: the console can also flag routes with sudden token growth and suggest caching or prompt trimming. there's an alerts tab for thresholds.
[05:44] [05:44] Sofia: a few questions we often get: Dedicated vs Hosted, when to pick Dedicated — cost predictability, SLA, and data isolation are main reasons. Hosted is good for quick time-to-value.
[05:59] Jason: ok for us predictability and residency are key, so Dedicated is attractive. what's the typical commit level?
[06:06] Liam: depends on throughput; for your peak traffic we'd model a commit that covers 60-70% of baseline and use burst capacity. we'll send a tailored proposal.
[06:16] [06:16] Priya: benchmark wise — we want to run a head-to-head for latency and cost on our sample workload. can redwood run benchmark tests in our env?
[06:25] Liam: we can run bench runs against a sandbox Dedicated cluster or provide a benchmark harness you can run. we'll include an example config (batching windows, concurrency, seq len distribution).
[06:36] Samir: the bench harness — does it simulate KV cache hit patterns?
[06:40] Liam: yes you can configure prefix cache hit rate; many customers see large gains when cache hit rate > 30% for chat.
[06:48] [06:48] Priya: any contract minimums for Dedicated?
[06:52] Sofia: usually monthly/annual commits depending on level; flexible pilot programs are available for POC.
[06:58] [07:00] Sofia: quick pause — folks, are there any blockers we haven't touched?
[07:06] Priya: one more: data residency — we need EU-only hosting for some endpoints.
[07:11] Liam: we support region pinning at route level and Private deployments can be deployed to your EU region; we'll document that.
[07:19] Jason: also curious about model variants and fallbacks in case of capacity constraints.
[07:24] Liam: console shows routing policies; you can specify fallbacks to quantized variants or lower-tier model families automatically. that's part of graceful degradation.
[07:34] [08:00] Sofia: moving on — I'm going to show the 'what-if' cost model in detail. here we add your traffic profile: avg reqs/day, median seq length, percent chat vs embeddings. then we toggle batching and quantization to show projected monthly savings.
[08:20] Priya: can we import sample logs?
[08:24] Liam: yes you can upload a sample usage CSV or hook into the usage API. we'll accept common schemas — again older exports sometimes have model name mismatch but we can map.
[08:36] [08:36] Jason: on the pricing side, will there be egress or network costs?
[08:41] Sofia: network egress is dependent on where you host. for Dedicated in your VPC, network costs are your cloud's. Redwood charges on per-token usage (or commit for Dedicated) plus optional add-ons. we'll share a cost model.
[09:00] Nina: do you support private control plane or full on-prem?
[09:04] Liam: Private control plane with customer-managed networking available; full on-prem packages exist for highly regulated customers but timeline and engineering effort are heavier. we'll scope it in the POC doc.
[09:16] [09:16] Priya: ok let's talk next steps real quick.
[09:20] Sofia: action items: we'll send pricing and pilot proposal, Liam will prepare POC scoping with benchmark config, and Aurora will share compliance checklist and preferred EU regions.
[09:31] Jason: timeline — we'll review internally next week and hope to reconvene for scoping mid-next week.
[09:37] Sofia: perfect. any other questions?
[09:40] Priya: none here. thanks for the walkthrough.
[09:43] Sofia: thanks everyone, I'll follow up with the doc links and pricing.
[09:47] [Screen share ends]
[09:50] End of meeting

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts — model names may be slightly off, e.g., 'rw-lama' instead of 'rw-llama'. export attachments: security pack link, pricing sheet (to be attached by AE).
